wall.text: The Berlin Wall was a guarded concrete barrier that divided Berlin from 1961 to 1989. It was constructed by East Germany starting on 13 August 1961. The Wall fell on 9 November 1989, after which East Germany opened its borders. Demolition of the wall began in June 1990 and was completed in 1992. The Brandenburg Gate stood in East Berlin near the wall.

eiffel.text: The Eiffel Tower is a wrought-iron lattice tower on the Champ de Mars in Paris, France. It is named after the engineer Gustave Eiffel, whose company designed and built the tower from 1887 to 1889. The tower is 330 metres tall, about the same height as an 81-storey building. It was the tallest man-made structure in the world until the Chrysler Building in New York City was finished in 1930. The tower has three levels for visitors, with restaurants on the first and second levels.

eiffel2.text: The Eiffel Tower is a wrought-iron lattice tower on the Champ de Mars in Paris. The tower is 324 metres tall including its antennas. The tower was built between 1887 and 1889 for the World's Fair.

pres.ref: Wikipedia — President of the United States
pres.text: Donald Trump is the 47th president of the United States, having taken office on January 20, 2025. He previously served as the 45th president from 2017 to 2021. Joe Biden served as the 46th president from 2021 to 2025. The president is both head of state and head of government.

mars.text: Mars has two small natural satellites, Phobos and Deimos. They were discovered in 1877 by Asaph Hall. Phobos is the larger of the two and orbits about 6,000 kilometres above the surface. Mars is the fourth planet from the Sun. Mars is not the largest of the terrestrial planets; Earth is larger.

waterloo.text: The Battle of Waterloo was fought on 18 June 1815 near Waterloo in present-day Belgium. A French army under Napoleon Bonaparte was defeated by two armies of the Seventh Coalition. The Duke of Wellington commanded the Anglo-allied army, and Field Marshal Blücher led the Prussian army. Napoleon abdicated four days later. Napoleon did not win the battle.

canberra.text: Canberra is the capital city of Australia. It is located in the Australian Capital Territory, between Sydney and Melbourne. Canberra is not the largest city of Australia; Sydney is the largest. The city was founded in 1913 and was selected as the capital in 1908 as a compromise between rivals Sydney and Melbourne. The population of Canberra is about 450,000.

einstein.text: Albert Einstein was born in Ulm, in the Kingdom of Württemberg in the German Empire, on 14 March 1879. He developed the theory of relativity. He received the 1921 Nobel Prize in Physics for his explanation of the photoelectric effect. Einstein moved to the United States in 1933 and died in Princeton, New Jersey, in 1955. He never returned to Germany.

crisis.text: The 2008 financial crisis was triggered by the collapse of the United States housing bubble. Lenders had issued many subprime mortgages, which were bundled into securities. When house prices fell, defaults rose and the securities lost value. Lehman Brothers filed for bankruptcy on 15 September 2008. As a result, credit markets froze and unemployment in the United States reached 10 percent in October 2009.

rome.ref: Wikipedia — Fall of the Western Roman Empire
rome.text: The Western Roman Empire fell in 476 AD when Odoacer deposed Romulus Augustulus. Historians point to many causes, including economic troubles, military defeats, and migration of Germanic peoples. The Eastern Roman Empire continued until 1453 when Constantinople fell to the Ottoman Empire.

gwall.text: The Great Wall of China is a series of fortifications built across the historical northern borders of ancient Chinese states. The total length of all sections ever built is 21,196 kilometres. The best-known sections were built by the Ming dynasty between 1368 and 1644. Construction of the earliest walls began in the 7th century BC. The wall is not visible to the naked eye from the Moon.

water.text: Water boils at 100 degrees Celsius at sea level, which is 212 degrees Fahrenheit. At higher altitude the boiling point is lower because air pressure is lower. At the summit of Mount Everest, water boils at about 71 degrees Celsius.

tokyo.text: Tokyo is the capital of Japan. The city proper has a population of about 14 million, and the Greater Tokyo Area has about 37 million people, making it the most populous metropolitan area in the world. Tokyo was formerly called Edo and was renamed in 1868. The Tokyo Metropolis covers 2,194 square kilometres.

pride.text: Pride and Prejudice is a novel by Jane Austen, published anonymously on 28 January 1813. The novel follows Elizabeth Bennet, the second of five daughters, and her relationship with Mr. Darcy. Austen wrote the first draft, titled First Impressions, between 1796 and 1797. The novel is set in rural England in the early 19th century.

pluto.text: Pluto is a dwarf planet in the Kuiper belt. It was discovered by Clyde Tombaugh in 1930 and was considered the ninth planet until 2006. In 2006 the International Astronomical Union defined a planet and Pluto did not meet the criteria, so it was reclassified as a dwarf planet. Pluto has five known moons, the largest being Charon.

apollo.text: Apollo 11 was the first crewed mission to land on the Moon. Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin landed the lunar module Eagle on 20 July 1969, while Michael Collins remained in orbit. Armstrong became the first person to walk on the Moon at 02:56 UTC on 21 July. The mission launched on 16 July 1969 from Kennedy Space Center in Florida. The crew returned to Earth on 24 July.

sky.ref: Britannica — Why is the sky blue
sky.text: The sky appears blue because of Rayleigh scattering. Sunlight reaches Earth's atmosphere and is scattered in all directions by gases and particles. Blue light is scattered more than red light because it travels as shorter, smaller waves. Therefore the sky looks blue during the day. At sunset the light passes through more atmosphere, so more of the blue is scattered away and the sky looks red.

committee.text: The committee had 12 members from the north, 7 from the south and 5 from the west. In total, the committee had 24 members. The committee met every Tuesday.

budget.text: The city spent 40 million dollars on roads, 25 million dollars on schools and 15 million dollars on parks, a total of 80 million dollars. The budget was approved in March.

seats.text: The party won 120 seats in the north and 80 seats in the south, giving it 200 seats overall. The opposition won 150 seats. Turnout was high in the north.

dino.text: Scientists believe an asteroid impact about 66 million years ago caused the extinction of the non-avian dinosaurs. The impact produced dust that blocked sunlight, which led to the collapse of food chains. The Chicxulub crater in Mexico is evidence of the impact.

scurvy.text: Scurvy is caused by a lack of vitamin C. Sailors on long voyages developed scurvy because they had no fresh fruit. James Lind showed in 1747 that citrus fruit cured the disease.

ozone.text: Chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs) damaged the ozone layer. The Montreal Protocol was signed in 1987, and as a result CFC production fell by about 98 percent. The ozone hole is expected to recover by around 2066 over Antarctica.

titanic.text: The RMS Titanic sank on 15 April 1912 after hitting an iceberg during her maiden voyage from Southampton to New York City. Of the 2,224 passengers and crew aboard, more than 1,500 died. There were too few lifeboats, so many could not escape.
